doc.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014

title: Writing film scores: arranger's piano, coffee shop and pencil
summary: He plays arranger's piano, scores in his head and on paper before Sibelius, and producers must trust him unheard.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Are you a keyboard player also?
I could get around. I don’t play classical music like Mozart, because I wasn’t trained like that, but I can certainly — I play what’s called arranger’s piano.
Yeah. So I can get around.
Because I was wondering, well how do you write — how did you write for the film if you’re not a real pianist.

I don’t think it’s necessary. I could write for — the last film I did I took a DVD player to a coffee shop and I watched the film and I scored it in a coffee shop. I hear it in my head. I gather the melodic material at home and I just write the melodies I want in certain parts of the film and then I just score it in my head. I know how it’s going to sound.
Using Finale or Sibelius or one of those things?

No. I go home and after — still my favorite process is score paper and a pencil. Because that’s how I learned. And then I transfer it into Sebelius. Because I’m very proficient in Sebelius now, the music program. So I score it in my head in a coffee shop, or I could do it right to Sebelius if I want but I like the 3-D. I like to get my hands filled with pencil smell you know.
I know. I just returned to that a couple of weeks ago and I said this feels good. The notes seem to mean more. © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

It’s three dimensional. You know? And then I’d go home and transfer it. So I don’t really use any sort of tools to orchestrate. I kind of look at the scene and I try to put forth the emotions that they want from that scene and I can hear it in my head, and then I score it.
And at what point do you run it by whoever can say yes or no? Before you get too far into it?

At no point could they really hear it. Because I tell them they can hear it if they want to, but they usually just leave it up to me for the session. Because if they hear it on my computer it’s going to sound like a bunch of noise to them. They’re not going to really hear how the real instruments are going to sound. They’re just going to hear a cheap imitation of how it’s going to sound. And it’s a lot of trust involved. There is major composers that have scored major films that had their scores thrown out by the producers before the movie was released obviously, but after the recording session. They just didn’t like it. And they would hire another composer to sit and —
Yeah. So they have money though. These producers have money you know.
Yeah. They’re probably insured for that.
